name: Cit Advanced

AGE (DAYS).reason: AutoGroup counts the current day as well, so its deal age reads one day higher than DMS's for the same deal. Confirmed as intended, not a defect. The relationship is verified on every record rather than the column being skipped, so a deal that stopped differing by exactly one day would still be reported.

_notes: screens holds paths only. The host comes from KPI_BASE_URL at run time, because this
file is committed and the tenant hostname is a customer's.
STATUS: CLEAN. The two screens agree completely on this module.
691 of 691 cells match — 688 record cells across 43 deals x 16 columns, plus 3 on the
lender table. No differences and nothing missing.
- 43 of those cells agreed under the declared AGE relationship (see recordColumns).
They are verified against it on every record, not skipped, so a deal that stopped
differing by exactly one day would be reported.
- The lender table matches AMOUNT FINANCED to the cent for all 3 lenders shown.
Note on run cost: neither screen documents formulas in tooltips (0 of 60 on AutoGroup,
0 of 266 on DMS), so the formula-harvest stage adds roughly ten minutes for nothing on
this module. Revealing every column made it markedly worse, since there are far more
tooltip-bearing cells to hover. Run this one with formula harvesting switched off.
What was wrong, for the record — none of it a data disagreement:
1. DMS renders a grand-total row inside the thead, below the real column names, so
columns were being identified by dollar figures. Fixed in columns.ts, which now
discards header rows holding figures rather than names.
2. DMS's listing was classified 'unknown' rather than 'detail', so the record-by-record
pass — the one that suits this module — never ran. It carries 14 descriptive columns
but 21 numeric GL columns alongside them, and the classifier's test was relative.
Fixed in structure.ts with an absolute descriptive-column signal.
3. Column headings ending in '?' ('B.O RECEIVED?') could not pair with their
counterpart ('BO RECEIVED') because '?' survived label normalization. Fixed in
match.ts. Worth 3 more paired columns here.
STILL OPEN: AutoGroup paginates its listing to 10 of 43 records, so 33 deals are not
compared at all. The capture reads the rendered page and never touches the paginator.
This is the single biggest remaining gap on this module, and it is also what prevents
confirming whether the AGE difference is definitional.
Columns left unpaired are all accounted for: CIT COUNT and the GL block are ignored by
decision, the second DMS AGE column has no counterpart by definition, and the row-number
columns identify nothing. SALESPERSON / SALES PERSON do not pair — a compound-word
difference the normalizer does not bridge — and they differ in substance anyway, since
AutoGroup lists every salesperson on a deal where DMS lists one.
_decisions: AGE: AutoGroup's single 'AGE (DAYS)' corresponds to the FIRST DMS 'AGE' column, which
is measured from Deal Date. The second DMS AGE column is measured from Acct Date and
has no AutoGroup counterpart. Across the 10 overlapping deals AutoGroup reads exactly
one higher than DMS (9 vs 8), consistent with inclusive counting on the AutoGroup
side. All 10 share the deal date 08/31/2026, so this is one date observed ten times,
not ten independent observations — re-confirm once the full 43 records are captured
before calling it definitional rather than an off-by-one defect.
CIT COUNT (AutoGroup): ignore. AutoGroup-only, no DMS counterpart to reconcile against.
DMS GL account columns: ignore. 210-VEHICLE ACCTS RECEIVABLE, 225-ALLOW FOR DOUBT
PAYOFFS and TOTAL are DMS-only detail.
FUNDED (AutoGroup card) is the same measure as 'Lender Received?' (DMS card). Both read
39. They should be compared as a pair.
Milestone timestamps are the same instants in different formats ('09/01/26 5:00 AM' vs
'09-01-2026 05:00 AM') and must be compared as timestamps. Compared as strings they
would report a difference on every deal.
DMS per-salesperson subtotal rows are skipped, not reconciled.
_resolved: AMOUNT FINANCED vs 205-CONTRACTS IN TRANSIT — RESOLVED from the data, not a discrepancy.
The gap is a general-ledger split, and it balances to the cent on all 43 deals:
- On 35 of 43, AMOUNT FINANCED - 205-CONTRACTS IN TRANSIT equals the row's TOTAL
column exactly (TOTAL carries the opposite sign). Deal 723831: gap 114.50,
- On the remaining 8, the residual is exactly the additional balances sitting in
210-VEHICLE ACCTS RECEIVABLE and 320-VEHICLE LIEN PAYOFFS. Deal 72823: residual
320 (-26,300). Every one of the 8 accounts for itself to the cent.
So amount financed is apportioned across GL accounts, with 205 holding the bulk and the
remainder in the other accounts. Nothing is missing on either screen.
Incidental observation: the gap never falls below 0.35% of amount financed, and sits at
exactly 0.35% on about half the deals, which looks like a standard percentage deduction
posted elsewhere. All 3 LEASE deals carry proportionally larger gaps (2.5-3.2%) than the
RETAIL ones.
CONSEQUENCE FOR THE COMPARISON: AMOUNT FINANCED <-> AMOUNT FINANCED is the correct
pairing and already matches exactly on all 43 deals. 205-CONTRACTS IN TRANSIT is a GL
component with no AutoGroup counterpart, so leaving it unpaired — as the GL block
already is by decision — is correct. Pairing it against AMOUNT FINANCED would have
manufactured 43 differences out of correct data.
_pending_engine_support: These decisions cannot be expressed in this file yet, and are recorded here rather
than written as config the engine would silently ignore:
- FUNDED <-> Lender Received? is an analytics-card pairing. compareTiles() takes no
aliases, so pairing it needs an engine change. Putting it under 'aliases' would
feed row matching instead and could mispair a row.
- Column-level ignore does not exist; 'ignore' applies to row labels only. The
AutoGroup-only and DMS-only columns above are already reported as unpaired columns,
which is honest, so this is cosmetic rather than blocking.
